bias: VIX crush and overnight rally as expected; NQ triggered the LBAF of Friday's low right at the open (held just off 200-221) and ran ~760 handles. But the close was weak and, despite the rip, today was an INSIDE day on a cash basis — so 'tomorrow's action is extremely consequential.' ES never took out Friday's low before rallying, which gives the least clarity possible on lower-first vs higher-first; the inside day makes it simple: treat today's RTH range as a box. Box trades: LBAF long, LAAF short, breakdown short with continuation, breakout long with continuation — any box trade is at least a B.
wildcard: Higher-than-usual chance ES prints an OUTSIDE day (takes both today's high and low, either order) — probable enough to mention, so be wary of the LAAF/LBAF trades once they get going. Full-session profile is a P after the cover rally: a breakdown of the body (today's low) risks a liquidation break all the way back down; a LAAF of the body targets today's low; a P can also break up. Box targets beyond today's range: up → Friday's open 7802.5 before Friday's high 7803.25 (red day); down → Friday's close 7702.75 before Friday's low 7676. Today's ES high was a partial back-test of the red multi-day range; SPX was a perfect back-test.

Any seller defense above today's high must trigger a LAAF (frankly a bearish engulfing of today's RTH range) or buyers have neutralized short timeframes and will buy the next dip for a higher low. Bearish-engulfing risk rises significantly back below 7753-54 after a LAAF of today's high. 60-65 and 53-54 are key from above in any LAAF.

Continuation below 7727.75 and 23-26 → 7706-12 becomes a 'must hold'; anything but a brief wick below it goes to the Sunday night low 7718.5 and Friday's low 7676, and today's high becomes another 30-min lower high. Keep Thursday's 7717.25 on the chart.
